Article Title: 'Will be dealt with iron hand': SC issues contempt notice to Kerala Congress over controversial CJI post
Article Text:
SC sends notice to Kerala Congress over CJI post

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court has issued a contempt notice to office-bearers of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) over a social media post targeting Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant, observing that freedom of expression cannot be used as a shield to interfere with the administration of justice.The apex court said, "Judgments are always open to criticism but freedom of expression can't be a shield for interference with administration of justice.""Any attempt to undermine authority of court needs to be dealt with iron hand," it further said, as cited by PTI.Reiterating the supremacy of the Constitution, the court added, "Constitution is supreme, no individual or political organisation stands above it."The Supreme Court has registered a petition based on a complaint seeking contempt proceedings against the KPCC over the social media post. According to the apex court's website, a complaint addressed to the CJI by advocate Vineet Jindal on October 13 was registered as a writ petition on October 30.The complaint also sought directions to authorities to ascertain whether a political demonstration and slogan-shouting held on the Supreme Court premises on the evening of October 12, 2026, involving Rahul Gandhi and other political leaders, took place without authorisation or caused any obstruction to the movement of advocates, litigants, judicial officers or court staff.A post targeting the CJI from the official Congress Kerala account on X went viral on October 12, drawing sharp criticism on social media, before being deleted. The party subsequently removed the person responsible for publishing it.In a statement, KPCC president Sunny Joseph said the person responsible for posting the controversial message on the party's official X account had been removed from the charge. He clarified that the post was made without the knowledge, consent or consultation of the KPCC leadership.Joseph also said the Congress party had no disagreement with regard to the impartiality of the judiciary.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court has issued a contempt notice to office-bearers of the Kerala Pradesh Congress Committee (KPCC) over a social media post targeting Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant. A post targeting the CJI from the official Congress Kerala account on X went viral on October 12, drawing sharp criticism on social media, before being deleted.

Article Title: 2013 Tehelka rape case: SC refuses to suspend Tarun Tejpal's 10-year jail term
Article Text:
Tejpal had approached the Supreme Court challenging the Bombay high court's August 6 judgment

What Tejpal argued

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Friday refused to suspend the 10-year prison sentence of former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal , convicted of raping a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in Goa in November 2013.A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale dismissed Tejpal's application after considering the evidence, including his emails and messages. The bench was of the view that no case had been made out for suspending his sentence, according to Live Law.Tejpal had approached the Supreme Court challenging the Bombay high court's August 6 judgment, which overturned his acquittal by a trial court in 2021 and convicted him in the case.Senior advocate Kapil Sibal, appearing for Tejpal, questioned the victim's account of the incident, particularly her claim that the elevator doors did not open during the alleged assault.Sibal argued that technical evidence showed the elevator doors opened twice during the two minutes and nine seconds in which the alleged incident took place. He said the hotel manager and Mitsubishi staff had testified that the lift doors opened automatically at every floor and could not be kept shut by pressing the buttons.He also questioned the investigation, alleging that the investigating officer failed to seize CCTV footage that could have established whether the elevator doors had opened.Tejpal's lawyers further argued that the victim had given six versions of the incident before the FIR was registered on November 22, 2013, and that none of them mentioned rape or oral penetration. They also stressed that Tejpal had remained on bail during the trial and had not misused his liberty.Solicitor general Tushar Mehta, appearing for the Goa government, opposed the plea and referred to messages and an apology email sent by Tejpal to the victim after the incident.Sibal countered that the apology had been drafted by then Tehelka editor Shoma Chaudhary and claimed it referred to a conversation between Tejpal and the woman, not an admission of rape.The case relates to allegations that Tejpal sexually assaulted a junior colleague inside an elevator at a luxury hotel during a Tehelka event in Goa in November 2013.A Goa trial court acquitted him in 2021. However, the Bombay High Court's Goa bench overturned the acquittal on August 6, 2026, convicted him of rape and other offences, and sentenced him to 10 years' rigorous imprisonment.
Article Summary: The Supreme Court refused to suspend the 10-year prison sentence of former Tehelka editor-in-chief Tarun Tejpal. He was convicted of raping a junior colleague inside a hotel elevator in Goa in November 2013. A bench of Justices MM Sundresh and Prasanna B Varale dismissed his application after considering the evidence.

NEW DELHI: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor on Friday said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations, asserting that President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback.Speaking in Thiruvananthapuram, Tharoor said the US election results would not change Washington's approach towards key issues such as tariffs, sanctions on countries buying Russian oil, the Iran war or the Ukraine conflict."Whether it comes to tariffs, whether it comes to sanctions for buying Russian oil, whether it comes to the Iran war itself, whether it comes to any initiative he takes on the Ukraine war. All of this, he's completely unaffected by the election result," Tharoor said.He explained that while Congress has significant powers over budgetary matters and can restrict or approve government spending, the President enjoys considerable discretion in foreign policy and international affairs.Tharoor said that even when it comes to military action, the President can proceed without seeking approval for an initial period of up to 60 days. However, Congress can exercise its financial powers to restrict expenditure, particularly in the case of an expensive military campaign."Those in India who are expecting this to have some impact on our relationship with the US, I think, are completely mistaken," he said.Commenting on the election outcome, Tharoor described it as an extraordinary setback for the ruling party, pointing out that midterm elections traditionally serve as a course correction for the party in power.He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin, including the election of a mayor of Indian origin in Los Angeles.Tharoor said the results reflected the vibrancy of American democracy but maintained that the outcome would not significantly alter Trump's ability to take decisions on international affairs.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor said the results of the US midterm elections would have little impact on India-US relations. He said President Donald Trump retains considerable powers to pursue his foreign policy agenda despite the ruling party's electoral setback. He also highlighted the gains made by candidates from minority communities and people of Indian origin.

NEW DELHI: NCP leader Praful Patel on Thursday visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital and enquired about his health. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups.The visit by Patel has triggered political speculation as he is among the NCP leaders reportedly "unhappy" with party boss Sunetra Pawar’s leadership. The meeting comes amid signs of internal discord within the party, adding a political dimension to Patel’s hospital visit.Sharad Pawar was admitted to Breach Candy Hospital on Wednesday night with a respiratory and chest infection, after being discharged from Pune’s Ruby Hall Clinic. Dr Pratit Samdani, a doctor at the hospital, said on Thursday that Pawar was stable and undergoing treatment."Sharad Pawar was admitted yesterday at Breach Candy Hospital for a respiratory and chest infection. He is stable and under treatment. He was admitted last night; he had a cough and an infection, something like bronchitis trouble. His treatment is ongoing, and he is currently stable," Dr Samdani told reporters.After meeting Pawar, Patel said the hospital admission was part of his routine medical check-ups and that his health was good. He also dismissed speculation that their meeting involved political discussions, saying he continued to meet Pawar and his daughter, Supriya Sule, because of their family ties.Also read: Rest, Supriya and I’ll look after country, PM Narendra Modi said to have told Sharad Pawar In a post on X, Patel said, "I visited the Breach Candy Hospital in Mumbai to pay a courtesy call on the esteemed Shri Sharad Pawar Saheb and inquired about his health."Providing an update on Pawar's condition, Patel said, "Sharad Pawar due to fatigue two days ago, was taken to Ruby Hall Clinic in Pune for a checkup. After that, he came to Mumbai, and here his health is fine. Naturally, a checkup happens once or twice a year, for a complete checkup, so in that context only he is admitted here at Breach Candy. His health is good. I am also happy that I came here, but everything is fine, and sahab was also in good spirits. He was asking about what is happening in politics in the country and state, as that is his interest. We had a good conversation, and I am happy that in a day or two all his checkups will be completed, so he will return home soon so he can rest."Patel also commented on Prime Minister Narendra Modi's conversation with Pawar, describing their relationship as long-standing and cordial. He said Modi's call to enquire about Pawar's health was natural given their association over the years.“Sharad Pawar and Narendra Modi have had a very long-standing relationship. I have also known Modi ji for many years and personally know about the relationship between him and Pawar sahab... I have witnessed their very good, cordial and respectful relationship over the years, even when we were in the UPA government in Delhi, and Modi ji was the Chief Minister of Gujarat... Modi ji is such a senior leader of the country today. So, if he received information about Sharad Pawar ji's health, it was natural for him to enquire about his well-being and speak to him...”Earlier, Pawar was admitted to Ruby Hall Clinic on November 2 after complaining of a cough and pleuritic chest pain. According to a statement issued by Dr Purvez K Grant, Chief Cardiologist, Chairman and Managing Trustee of the hospital, Pawar was stable and doing well at the time of his discharge."Mr Sharad Pawar has been discharged from Ruby Hall Clinic today. He is stable and doing well. He will be travelling directly from the hospital to his residence in Mumbai. We wish him good health and a speedy recovery," the statement said.His daughter, Baramati MP and NCP (SP) working president Supriya Sule, had earlier said that Pawar was undergoing medical tests and that his health parameters were stable. Ruby Hall Clinic subsequently said he would remain under observation as a precautionary measure. Doctors cleared him for discharge after his condition remained stable and his discomfort subsided.The developments come amid growing concerns within the BJP over organisational differences in its ally -- NCP. Union home minister Amit Shah met several senior NCP functionaries late Sunday who are believed to be unhappy with party president Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth, and urged them to resolve their differences in the party’s interest.Those who met Shah included NCP national working president Praful Patel, Maharashtra unit chief Sunil Tatkare, ministers Chhagan Bhujbal and Hasan Mushrif, and leaders Dhananjay Munde and Dilip Patil. Deputy chief minister Sunetra Pawar and her son Parth were absent from the meeting.Following the meeting, Sunetra Pawar convened a core committee meeting in Mumbai.
Article Summary: NCP leader Praful Patel visited Nationalist Congress Party (SP) chief Sharad Pawar at Mumbai’s Breach Candy Hospital. Patel said the veteran politician was stable and expected to return home in a day or two after completing his medical check-ups. NEW DELHI: National Conference supremo Farooq Abdullah on Friday dismissed reports of divisions within the party as “completely false”, asserting that the organisation remained "united and could not be broken. Article Title: Kashmir has 1 active local terrorist, says IG
Article Text:
Inspector General of Police (IGP) Kashmir Zone, Sujit Kumar speaks during a press conference, in Srinagar

Valley recruitment stopped this year: Police chief

SRINAGAR: Kashmir has just one active local terrorist and recruitment in the valley completely stopped this year, while security forces were tracking a handful of foreign terrorists believed to be assisting him, J&K police IG Sujit Kumar said Thursday.Police identified the lone local terrorist as Mohammad Lateef Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chader village in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district. A Rs 15 lakh reward was announced in Aug for information leading to his arrest. Bhat is accused of killing a head constable and two migrant workers in separate attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam in July. He is believed to have joined terrorist ranks last year.“No local has joined terrorist ranks this year. Local recruitment has completely dried up,” Kumar said. He added that the number of foreign terrorists could not be established as they kept moving between locations. “Giving their figure would be an exaggeration,” he said.Head constable Ashiq Hussain’s murder on July 22 was the first terrorist attack in Kashmir since the massacre of 25 tourists and a local pony operator in Pahalgam on April 22 last year.On restrictions imposed on civilian traffic during Army convoy movement since the Pahalgam attack, Kumar said security protocols reflected past terrorist strikes and continuing threat inputs. He said the matter was on the radar and would be discussed with other agencies. On Oct 30, health minister Sakina Itoo had flagged ambulances being stuck and students missing classes because of highway closures during security transit.On narcoterrorism, Kumar said police registered 1,651 NDPS cases this year, arrested 1,941 people, seized 1,711 kg of contraband and over Rs 1 crore in cash. Properties worth Rs 154 crore were attached and 567 bank accounts frozen.
Article Summary: Police identified the lone local terrorist as Mohammad Lateef Bhat, a resident of Khrewan Chader village in south Kashmir’s Kulgam district. Bhat is accused of killing a head constable and two migrant workers in separate attacks in Anantnag and Kulgam in July.

Union parliamentary affairs minister Kiren Rijiju on Wednesday took a swipe at Congress leader Rahul Gandhi , listing seven conditions that he said the opposition party should follow if it wants to "win more MPs".In a post on X, Rijiju said Gandhi should spend more time in India, avoid meeting people he described as "anti-India" and stop promoting their agenda. He also urged the Congress leader to respect senior leaders and learn from their experience, saying it was part of Indian tradition.Listing the conditions, Rijiju asked Gandhi to "spend more time in India and avoid secret foreign vacations frequently."He further advised him to "end deep hatred against BJP, RSS and Modi Ji" and "treat BJP as political opponent, not enemy."The minister also asked Gandhi to take "Parliament more seriously" and allow MPs to participate in debates and discussions."Respect Constitution of India, and honour Constitutional Institutions, and allow Congress party to function as a democratic party and smash dynastic politics," he said, listing the final two conditions.Rijiju's remarks came amid an ongoing exchange between the ruling BJP and the Congress over Rahul Gandhi's demand for an open debate with Prime Minister Narendra Modi.Earlier on Wednesday, Rijiju shared a video clip of his speech in Parliament during which opposition leaders had walked out of the House."Parliament is the House for debates & discussion. But people who don't believe in democracy, debates and discussion are talking about debate," the parliamentary affairs minister said.Meanwhile, Rahul renewed his challenge to Modi for an open debate, claiming that he could establish within five minutes that the prime minister was a traitor. His remarks drew a sharp response from Union Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman.Following Rahul's challenge, Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also urged the prime minister to come forward and answer questions raised over alleged vote theft.In a post on X, Kharge said Modi had no answers on the "vote chori" issue and should accept Gandhi's challenge to debate various subjects, including "foreign connections"."You don't come to Parliament. You have not done a SINGLE OPEN PRESS CONFERENCE; it's time you came for a DEBATE.“Come forward, Face Questions. Tell the Nation why did you indulge in VOTE CHORI !!” Kharge said.“PM Modi is parroting his flop line of ‘Dimaagi Naxal’! He has NO answer on Vote Chori and the Open Challenge by Rahul Gandhi to discuss how he mortgaged Indian interests to Foreign powers!” he added.Kharge also questioned Home Minister Amit Shah's remarks about three crore voters being "ghuspaithiyas" (infiltrators), asking what he had been doing as home minister if illegal immigrants had entered the country.“He should be sacked for his incompetence,” the Congress president said.Responding to Rahul's challenge, Sitharaman said Parliament was already an appropriate venue for a debate and reminded him that he was the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha."Rahul ji, you ask the Prime Minister to choose a venue for a debate. There is already one: Parliament, where you happen to be the LoP."Just yesterday, Home Minister Shri Amit Shah offered a special session to debate SIR and EVMs. Why not show the same enthusiasm for a debate in Parliament that you show while issuing challenges on social media?" Sitharaman said on X.She said that demanding answers also required Rahul to stay and hear the government's response."Demanding answers also carries an obligation to hear them," she said, alleging that Gandhi and other Congress leaders had walked out of Parliament on several occasions while the government was responding to their allegations.Sitharaman also accused the Congress and its INDIA bloc allies of repeatedly disrupting parliamentary proceedings, resulting in entire sittings being washed out.She further questioned the nature of Gandhi's allegations and asked him to present specific claims backed by evidence."Simply throwing together a long list of accusations doesn’t make your case any stronger. As LoP, you are expected to show some seriousness and responsibility."You say, 'Daro mat'. Then bring the facts, face the scrutiny and stay to hear the answers. In the House, uphold the standards of debate you demand from others," she said.
Article Summary: Kiren Rijiju lays down 7 conditions for Rahul, takes swipe at Congress leader. Gandhi should spend more time in India, avoid meeting people he described as "anti-India" Gandhi should respect senior leaders and learn from their experience, he said. Gandhi renewed his challenge to Modi for an open debate.

NEW DELHI: The Jharkhand High Court on Friday quashed the state government's decision to cancel the Jharkhand Staff Selection Commission Combined Graduate Level (JSSC CGL) examination, bringing relief to candidates who had cleared the recruitment test.The court also set aside the government's decision to cancel the recruitment advertisement for the appointments, according to news agency ANI.The ruling comes amid ongoing legal proceedings over the cancellation of several recruitment examinations in Jharkhand following allegations of irregularities and weeks of protests by candidates.On August 18, the Jharkhand government issued a notification cancelling 22 recruitment examinations, including the 11th to 13th Jharkhand Public Service Commission (JPSC) examinations, following public protests over alleged irregularities.Two days later, on August 20, the Jharkhand High Court stayed the state government's order cancelling the appointments of government employees recruited through the 11th to 13th JPSC examinations.The high court had earlier deferred hearings on petitions challenging the cancellation of JPSC and JSSC recruitment examinations and appointments, scheduling the next hearing for September 18.The court fixed the date after the state government sought additional time to file its affidavit.The government had previously been directed to submit the affidavit by September 7 but failed to do so within the stipulated period.The cancellation of the JSSC CGL examination had triggered protests by candidates, including those who had already secured government appointments through the recruitment process.In a protest held after the cancellation announcement, appointed candidates questioned the government's decision and demanded an opportunity to present their side.One of the protesters, Chanda Kumari, told news agenct PTI that thousands of candidates who had secured appointments had been affected by the decision.She questioned whether cancelling the examination would ensure justice and action against those actually responsible for the alleged irregularities.“Our judiciary and democracy function on the principle that even if 100 guilty people go free, one innocent person should not be punished. But with the government's decision, thousands of innocent people have been punished immediately,” she said.Student leader Devendra Nath Mahto, who had been on a 16-day hunger strike, ended his protest after the government announced the cancellations. He described the decision as a “huge victory for Jharkhand” but said his campaign for recruitment reforms would continue, the earlier report said.Meanwhile, the Jharkhand Criminal Investigation Department (CID) has arrested two accused in separate cases linked to alleged irregularities in competitive examinations, officials said.In connection with alleged irregularities in the 14th JPSC preliminary examination, the CID arrested Sanjeet Kumar from the Ratu Road area of Ranchi.Kumar, who allegedly ran Shivangan Coaching Centre, is accused of acting as an agent and collecting money from candidates by promising to help them clear the examination, officials said.The alleged irregularities have also reached the Supreme Court. Last month, the apex court issued notices to the Centre, the Jharkhand government and others on a public interest litigation seeking a Central Bureau of Investigation (CBI) or an independent probe into alleged irregularities in the 2025 JPSC Civil Services Preliminary Examination.A bench comprising Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana sought responses from the authorities on the petition filed by social worker Harisharan Devgan.Senior advocate Manan Kumar Mishra, appearing for the petitioner, told the bench that students had been continuously protesting over the alleged irregularities.The petitioner has sought directions for a fresh preliminary examination under safeguards approved by the Supreme Court.
Article Summary: Jharkhand High Court quashes state government's decision to cancel recruitment test. Ruling comes amid ongoing legal proceedings over the cancellation of several recruitment examinations. Jharkshand Criminal Investigation Department (CID) arrests two accused in separate cases linked to alleged irregularities in competitive examinations.

If Parliament reconvenes, I believe Rahul Gandhi's offer to debate still stands," Tharoor said.Tharoor also criticised the Election Commissiono ver its handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls, alleging procedural irregularities and saying the Supreme Court hearings had supported the Opposition's concerns.Commenting on the ECI's decision to de-link the SIR declaration from Form 6, Tharoor described it as one of the Commission's "most outrageous mistakes". He alleged that the ECI, under Chief Election Commissioner Gyanesh Kumar, had made unauthorised changes to electoral procedures and permitted the bulk filing of Form 7 objections, resulting in people being denied their voting rights."The ordinary public has not fully understood all of these examples of frankly bureaucratic and administrative malfeasance that were conducted by the Election Commission under Gyanesh Kumar.Some of these things were objected to by the two other Election Commissioners as well. One of them is Form Six, where you suddenly unilaterally change the form, introducing a new declaration which is not authorized under the rules and laws of the country. ..This is what the opposition was complaining about...Under this election commission, bulk filling of Form 7s with thousands of names has been permitted, including in states like West Bengal. And as a result, on the basis of mere suspicion, a large number of people were denied the right to vote."Tharoor said the Opposition had sought not only Kumar's resignation but also a reversal of decisions taken during the SIR exercise that had allegedly affected eligible voters. He welcomed the ECI's move to roll back some of its decisions but said the consequences of earlier actions also needed to be reversed."But what has been done by the Election Commission now to roll back some of their mistakes, that is one of the things we asked for. We wanted not just Mr. Gyanesh Kumar's resignation; we wanted very much that the electoral process under the SIR should be reversed, that you should actually end up with these wrong decisions cancelled and their consequences for innocent Indian citizens be reversed...We've had an extraordinary number of 113 million votes cut from the register. For all of these reasons, what the Election Commission did was wrong; we have been saying it is wrong and the hearings in the Supreme Court are clearly demonstrating step by step that we were right and they were wrong," he said.Tharoor's remarks came amid a political confrontation between the Congress and the BJP over allegations of vote theft and the functioning of the Election Commission.On Thursday, Union Home Minister Amit Shah challenged Rahul Gandhi to debate the allegations in Parliament, urging him to present his arguments in the House rather than take the political battle to the streets. Addressing a rally in Karnal, Haryana, Shah said Gandhi would not be able to handle the government's response."If you (Rahul Gandhi) wish to engage in a responsible discussion—if your concerns hold truth, substance, and logic—then come and discuss them inside Parliament. Let’s face each other head-on! But you won’t be able to handle the answers; as always, you will just run away," Shah said.Shah's challenge followed Rahul's call for an open debate with Prime Minister Narendra Modi a day earlier. The Congress leader had claimed he could prove within five minutes that the prime minister was a "deshdrohi" (traitor).Congress president Mallikarjun Kharge also urged Modi to answer questions surrounding alleged vote theft. Responding to Rahul's challenge, Finance Minister Nirmala Sitharaman said Parliament was already the appropriate forum for such a debate and reminded him of his responsibilities as the Leader of the Opposition in the Lok Sabha.
Article Summary: Congress MP Shashi Tharoor backs Rahul Gandhi's offer to debate the government's allegations in Parliament. Says the House should reconvene as it has not yet been prorogued. Criticises the Election Commissiono ver its handling of the Special Intensive Revision (SIR) of electoral rolls.

Around a decade and a half before Los Angeles elected her as its first Indian-origin mayor, Kerala-born Tamil Nithya Raman sat with residents of a south Chennai suburb to map the notorious traffic snarls that would routinely disrupt their lives.On Thursday, WhatsApp groups in Nanganallur were buzzing with messages claiming the face riding the crest of the blue wave along Southern California's glitziest skyline as one of their own.Someone wrote in about being part of the group of 10-odd residents she interacted with regularly as an urban planner helping find solutions to the suburb's civic problems. I am her oldest surviving relative here," said Vanaja, showing family albums containing her now-famous niece's pictures.Nithya (45) moved to Louisiana with her parents as a six-year-old and became a US citizen by 22. Armed with an urban planning degree from Harvard University, she arrived in Chennai at 23 and founded Transparent Chennai, a civic initiative under Centre for Development Finance at Institute for Financial Management and Research. It used data and community participation to tackle urban governance.Nithya worked on urban planning in Chennai from 2004 to 2013, including working closely with local citizens' groups to document civic problems."The collaboration involved organising community forums, mapping traffic problems and collecting data on public transport, pedestrian safety and gaps in civic infrastructure," said V Rama Rao, an activist from Lakshmi Nagar in Nanganallur. "The data was meant to be presented to Chennai traffic police and municipal corporations to help develop actionable solutions."Nithya has acknowledged her Chennai stint in interviews to international publications, saying her organisation mapped and evaluated public toilets across the city to identify what needed to be fixed. She also spoke about studying working conditions of recycling workers and helping them get recognition from the state govt.In Thiruvananthapuram, where Nithya was born in 1981, aunt Vanaja said her niece loved visiting Kovalam for its beach and prayed at the Sree Padmanabhaswamy temple. "Nithya studied at a private school in Thrissur before moving to the US. She likes leading a simple life and has a lot of empathy for the poor. Perhaps it was this quality that led her to public life in the US."Before immigrating to the US, Nithya's father, R Venkataraman, worked at Keltron while her mother, Sudha, was emploted with Indian Overseas Bank.
Article Summary: Nithya Raman is the first Indian-origin mayor of a major U.S. city. The 45-year- old moved to Louisiana with her parents when she was six. Article Title: Delhi riots case: Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam challenge Delhi HC's bail refusal in Supreme Court
Article Text:

NEW DELHI: Jailed activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have separately moved the Supreme Court challenging the Delhi high court's September 30 order refusing them bail in the 2020 Delhi riots larger conspiracy case.In their pleas, both activists argue that they should be granted bail as the prosecution has failed to examine a single witness despite them having spent more than six years in custody as an undertrial. They also pointed out that the one-year period stipulated by the Supreme Court for filing fresh bail pleas was nearing its end.The petition by Imam stated that the chargesheet in the case was filed on September 25, 2020, naming 18 accused and citing more than 900 witnesses, including 47 protected witnesses. However, the prosecution is yet to examine even one witness, Imam submitted.Khalid in his plea pointed out that the prosecution has failed to examine protected witnesses and the one-year embargo imposed by the top court is about to expire and therefore prolonged incarceration would violate Article 21 of the Constitution.Article 21 of the Constitution asserts that no person shall be deprived of their life except according to the procedure established by law.This means that every individual has the right to live, and their life cannot be taken away except in accordance with the prescribed legal procedures.The Delhi high court on September 30 rejected the fresh bail pleas of Khalid and Imam, holding that it was bound by judicial discipline and could not modify the Supreme Court's January 5 order. The top court had allowed the two to approach the courts again after the examination of protected witnesses or after the expiry of one year, whichever came earlier.The two activists had approached the high court after a trial court rejected their bail applications for the third time on July 4. The trial court had said it had "no option but to follow" the Supreme Court's January 5 order and could neither entertain their pleas nor grant relief.During the high court proceedings, senior advocate Trideep Pais, appearing for Khalid, had argued that there were three "small changes in circumstances" since the earlier proceedings. He pointed out that charges had not yet been framed and prosecution witnesses had not been examined. Pais also relied on a Supreme Court judgment to support his submissions.Opposing the pleas, Delhi police maintained that Khalid and Imam were the "masterminds" of the riots and could not seek bail on parity with other accused. The police argued that the Supreme Court had previously categorised them as part of the alleged conspiracy's "command authority" and held that their risk profiles justified continued detention.On January 5, the Supreme Court upheld the Delhi high court's September 2, 2025 decision denying bail to Khalid and Imam, while granting relief to five co-accused — Gulfisha Fatima, Meeran Haider, Shifa Ur Rehman, Mohammad Saleem Khan and Shadab Ahmad.A bench of Justices Aravind Kumar and N V Anjaria had observed that there was a prima facie case against Khalid and Imam under the Unlawful Activities (Prevention) Act (UAPA). It also noted that their alleged roles were distinct from those of the other accused, describing them as the "ideological drivers" of the alleged conspiracy.Khalid and Imam have been in custody since September 2020 and August 2020, respectively. They are accused of being among the masterminds of the larger conspiracy behind the February 2020 riots in northeast Delhi, which left 53 people dead and more than 700 injured.The violence erupted amid protests against the Citizenship (Amendment) Act (CAA) and the proposed National Register of Citizens (NRC).The Supreme Court has previously also referred to a larger bench the question of prolonged incarceration of undertrials booked under the UAPA in view of the law's stringent bail conditions.
Article Summary: Jailed activists Umar Khalid and Sharjeel Imam have separately moved the Supreme Court. They are challenging the Delhi high court's September 30 order refusing them bail in the 2020 Delhi riots larger conspiracy case. Both activists argue that they should be granted bail as the prosecution has failed to examine a single witness.

CHENNAI: The Indian Medical Association (IMA) has asked the Central Board of Film Certification (CBFC) to refuse certification to the Hindi film Suryaa: Ant Se Aarambh Tak, starring Sunny Deol and Ravi Kishan, which is slated for release on Nov 20.The IMA objects to the film's teaser, released on Oct 19. In it, a father who has lost his daughter says doctors "write commission slips" instead of prescriptions, then asks how long people will tolerate this. The teaser then shows him assaulting doctors and nursing staff members inside a hospital, which the IMA says is presented as a heroic and justified act.In a representation dated Nov 4, IMA national president Dr Anilkumar J Nayak urged the board to deny certification under Section 4(2)(v) read with Section 5B(1) of the Cinematograph Act, 1952, and the 2026 certification guidelines.The association said the objectionable content is the film's core theme and cannot be removed by mere excisions.The IMA wants the board to refuse certification to any trailer, teaser or promotional material that shows violence against doctors, nurses or hospital staff, or carries dialogue imputing corruption to doctors as a class.It has sought a screening under Section 7C for IMA representatives, the presence of an IMA-nominated medical expert when the examining committee views the film, and a hearing before any decision is taken.It said if any certificate is recommended, the chairperson should refer the film to a revising committee under Rule 25(1) of the Cinematograph (Certification) Rules, 2024. It wants every scene showing violence against healthcare workers as justified or heroic deleted, along with the dialogue on corruption. It also wants a prominent disclaimer that the film does not represent the medical profession and that such violence is punishable.The association asked for a written, reasoned decision and priority consideration given the release date. It reserved the right to approach the courts.
Article Summary: The IMA objects to the film's teaser, released on Oct 19. In it, a father who has lost his daughter says doctors "write commission slips" instead of prescriptions. One officer was killed and three others wounded in a firefight with a suspect in Lakewood, a suburb of Denver, Colorado, on Thursday evening. The suspect was also fatally shot by police during the exchange of gunfire.The shooting took place around 6.30pm when Lakewood police officers reached the bus following a call about the suspicious person, police spokesperson John Romero said during a news conference. Another person was also injured in the incident, although the circumstances surrounding their injury remain unclear, Romero said.Police said the suspect may have been involved in a hit-and-run incident earlier in the day. However, authorities have not released his identity or provided further details about the possible connection.Lakewood Police are investigating the shooting and have urged the public to stay away from the area.The identities of the deceased officer, the injured officers and the suspect have not yet been made public.The Regional Transportation District (RTD), which operates public transport services in the area, said it was deeply concerned about the shooting.“RTD personnel responded to the incident immediately and are fully cooperating with the Lakewood Police Department as it conducts its investigation,” the statement said.

Article Title: 'Long road ahead': Eisenkot beats Netanyahu 67-46 in backing but government test looms
Article Text:
Although Eisenkot received recommendations from more than the 61 lawmakers required for a Knesset majority, the Israeli President Herzog has not yet formally assigned him the mandate to form the government.

Forming a government remains difficult for Netanyahu's rival

Herzog to hold further consultations

Poll Vote & Share your view What do you think will be the biggest challenge for Gadi Eisenkot in forming Israel's next government? Israel's Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot has secured the backing of 67 members of the Knesset to receive the mandate to form Israel's next government. This has also put him ahead of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu.However, despite the strong endorsement, Eisenkot faces a difficult task in building a coalition. Several parties that are backing his candidature are also unwilling to join his government.Eisenkot secured the support during consultations with Israeli President Isaac Herzog on Thursday, after the Arab-led Joint List unanimously decided to recommend him for the prime ministerial mandate. He has reiterated his goal of forming a "national emergency government" to bring political stability to Israel.In a post on X, Eisenkot said the first round of discussions with the opposition parties had concluded with an absolute majority of recommendations in his favour. He, however, acknowledged that the road to forming a government remained long."First round of talks and meetings this week with the Change and Repair parties. This evening, the round of consultations at the President's Residence was completed with an absolute majority of recommenders for the purpose of receiving the mandate from the President of the State to form a government.The goal: The establishment of a national emergency government that will return our dear country to safety and sanity. The road ahead of us is still long; we are very determined. We will do it, and we will succeed," he wrote.Eisenkot's 67 endorsements comprise 48 lawmakers from the Jewish-led opposition bloc, including Yashar, Together, The Democrats and Yisrael Beiteinu. The Ra'am party contributed eight seats, while the Joint List added 11.Netanyahu, meanwhile, received recommendations from only 46 lawmakers, down from the 53 seats previously expected to back him. His traditional ally, United Torah Judaism (UTJ), refused to recommend either candidate, leaving the prime minister with a reduced tally.According to a report by Times of Israel, the Joint List's decision proved crucial in giving Eisenkot a decisive lead over Netanyahu. The party had earlier indicated that it might abstain but eventually announced its support during Thursday's consultations.Joint List chairman Yousef Jabareen defended the move, saying the party wanted to prevent Netanyahu from returning to power."We will do everything to remove the greatest threat to all of us, which is the continuation of the rule of Netanyahu and his Kahanist partners," he said in a post on X.Despite crossing the 61-seat majority mark during the presidential consultations, Eisenkot's endorsements do not necessarily translate into support for an actual governing coalition.The Joint List has made clear that it has significant policy disagreements with parts of the Jewish opposition's platform. It has also ruled out formally joining an Eisenkot-led coalition, although it could support the government from outside.The Times of Israel reported that only 48 of the 67 lawmakers who recommended Eisenkot are currently prepared to work together without conditions. This is five fewer than the 53-seat bloc Netanyahu was expected to command before UTJ withheld its recommendation.The possibility of securing UTJ's support also presents difficulties. The ultra-Orthodox party is a key player in the dispute over exemptions from military service for Haredi men. Its demands on the issue are at odds with the positions of several parties in Eisenkot's camp.Yisrael Beiteinu leader Avigdor Liberman has also ruled out forming a government that depends on support from Arab parties, making it harder for Eisenkot to rely on the Joint List and Ra'am.The Times of Israel noted that Netanyahu and his allies could also use the prospect of an opposition government relying on Arab party support to undermine Eisenkot's political ambitions. The Likud-led campaign questioning the legitimacy of Arab political participation could intensify if such an arrangement takes shape.Eisenkot now has the political momentum, but converting the recommendations into a workable majority will be his biggest challenge. Unlike Netanyahu, who has a long record of navigating complex coalition negotiations, Eisenkot has relatively little experience in political horse-trading.Although Eisenkot received recommendations from more than the 61 lawmakers required for a Knesset majority, the Israeli President Herzog has not yet formally assigned him the mandate to form the government.According to ANI, the president will hold further consultations with political parties before deciding on Sunday whom to task with forming the next government.According to the Times of Israel report, Herzog had also attempted to explore the possibility of a national unity arrangement during Thursday's meetings. However, Eisenkot's camp signalled its opposition to sharing power with Netanyahu.
Article Summary: Israel's Yashar party leader Gadi Eisenkot has secured the backing of 67 members of the Knesset to receive the mandate to form Israel's next government. This has also put him ahead of Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu. However, he faces a difficult task in building a coalition. Several parties backing his candidature are also unwilling to join his government.

Article Title: Tourists pay up to ₹200 entry fee at Chandradrona hills, but Manikyadhara has no drinking water, functional toilet or changing room for women
Article Text:
Peak Neglect: Mullayyanagiri peak in the Chandradrona hill range has nodrinking water, and the road to it from Kaimara has no road signs or streetlights





Chikkamagaluru: Despite the district administration and tourism department collecting entry fees from tourists visiting Chandradrona hill stations, the area continues to lack basic facilities.There is no drinking water, functional toilet or changing room for women at Manikyadhara atop the hills.Hundreds of vehicles daily cross Kaimara, the gateway to the Chandra Drona hill range that houses Mullayyanagiri, Dattapitha and Manikyadhara. The fee is Rs 50 for a bike, Rs 100 for a car, Rs 150 for an SUV, and Rs 200 for a Tempo Traveller.During the peak tourist season, monthly toll collection comes to nearly Rs 45 lakh. Yet, visitors continue to be hobbled by lack of basic facilities.Karnataka Rakshana Vedike (Shivaramegowda faction) workers staged a protest recently over lack of facilities. “For six months, we staged a symbolic protest -- half-clad – and handed memorandums to govt officials concerned. Yet, no one listened to us,” said Sumanth, the Vedike district president.The road from Kaimara to Mullayyanagiri has no road signs or streetlights.There is no drinking water at Mullayyanagiri or Seethalayyanagiri. At Manikyadhara waterfalls, where devotees bathe, there is no changing room for women. They are forced to change clothes in vehicles. There are no dustbins, no medical centre, and no police outpost despite a 5,000-plus footfall on weekends, he alleged.“Tourists are going back with bad memories and are unlikely to return due to these inconveniences,” said Raghunath, a homestay owner.Tourists say they’re not against fee collection. “We will happily pay Rs 200 if you provide a clean toilet, sufficient drinking water, and parking space,” said a biker group from Mysuru.Tourism officials claim a proposal to build toilets, drinking water dispensers, changing rooms and to carry out road repair work has been sent to the department and work is expected to start soon.Despite this assurance, there is no official timeline yet to carry out the works for much-needed civic amenities at the site.
Article Summary: There is no drinking water, functional toilet or changing room for women at Manikyadhara. The road from Kaimara to Mullayyanagiri has no road signs or streetlights. There are no dustbins, no medical centre, and no police outpost despite a 5,000-plus footfall on weekends.

Article Text:
Arab communities celebrate El-Sayed’s historic US Senate victory

Poll Vote & Share your view Should candidates in the US Senate incorporate cultural expressions from their heritage into their public speeches? Absolutely! No, they should keep it professional. 3k+ users shared opinion today 5k+ users already voted today 3k+ users shared opinion today Share Opinion

Abdul El-Sayed’s historic election as the first Muslim American to the US Senate has sparked celebrations among Arab communities, with supporters across the US and the Middle East embracing his use of Arabic expressions such as “habibi” and “inshallah” in American political discourse.El-Sayed, the son of Egyptian immigrants, drew widespread attention with his victory speech, in which he mocked US Vice President JD Vance over his earlier criticism of the Democratic candidate. Addressing Vance, he said, “JD, habibi,” before pointing out that the vice president would be constitutionally required to swear him in when the Senate convenes in January.“Habibi”, which literally means “my beloved”, is commonly used as a term of affection and can also mean “buddy” or “pal” in everyday conversation. The expression became a popular campaign slogan, with supporters wearing T-shirts bearing the words “Habibi for Abdul”.El-Sayed also spoke about how his campaign had turned “inshallah”, meaning “God willing”, into “hamdulillah”, or “thank God”, following his election victory. His use of Arabic expressions resonated with supporters, prompting celebrations and a wave of social media posts featuring Arabic music and cultural references.The celebrations were particularly significant for Arab and Muslim communities, which have faced decades of prejudice and Islamophobic rhetoric in the United States. During the campaign, El-Sayed was subjected to attacks from President Donald Trump and other Republicans. Trump called him a “jihadist” and a “communist”, invoked the September 11 attacks and repeatedly mispronounced his name.Responding to the criticism in his victory speech, El-Sayed said, “Donald, look, I know you've struggled with my name. So after JD swears me in in January, you can just go on and call me ‘senator.'”The 42-year-old epidemiologist, who was born in Michigan to Egyptian immigrant parents, has frequently spoken about his Egyptian heritage, including his family's food and humour and his childhood memories of spending summers in Alexandria, where his father grew up.El-Sayed defeated Republican candidate and former representative Mike Rogers in one of the country's closely watched Senate races. His victory came after he secured the Democratic nomination by defeating Representative Haley Stevens in the party's primary earlier this year.His campaign was centred on progressive policies, including universal healthcare through the Medicare for All proposal and an end to US military aid to Israel. However, he faced a setback in the final days of the campaign when Stevens withdrew her support and endorsed Rogers after attending church with the Republican candidate.Republicans had sought to portray the contest as a referendum on the Democratic Party's progressive wing. Despite the attacks and the withdrawal of Stevens' support, El-Sayed secured the Senate seat, extending the Republican Party's electoral drought in Michigan. Republicans have not won a Senate seat in the state since 1994.El-Sayed will succeed retiring Democratic Senator Gary Peters. His victory was among several electoral breakthroughs for women, candidates of colour and other underrepresented groups in the November 3 midterm elections, in which Democrats also made significant gains in key statewide races and flipped control of both chambers of Congress.
Article Summary: Abdul El-Sayed is the first Muslim American elected to the US Senate. His victory has sparked celebrations among Arab communities. Supporters embraced his use of Arabic expressions such as “habibi” and “inshallah” in American political discourse.

Article Title: Two years after Donald Trump's conviction on 34 felony counts over a $130,000 payment to Stormy Daniels, his lawyers ask a New York appeals court to overturn the verdict on immunity and legal grounds
Article Text:
Trump's lawyers questioned jury unanimity requirements, while prosecutors highlighted the defence's earlier acceptance of the judge's instructions.

Lawyers challenge the legal foundation of the conviction

Presidential immunity becomes another battleground

Judges question both sides as Trump continues his fight

US President Donald Trump is once again under judicial scrutiny. Nearly two years after a New York jury found him guilty of 34 felony counts connected to a hush money payment made before the 2016 presidential election, Trump's legal team is attempting to have the historic verdict overturned. The latest challenge brought the President's lawyers face to face with a five-judge appeals panel, which closely examined questions surrounding presidential immunity, election laws and the evidence presented during his trial.According to AP News, Trump's attorneys appeared before a New York appellate court on Thursday, November 5, arguing that the conviction should be overturned because the prosecution relied on federal election law to elevate the charges from misdemeanours to felonies.The case originated from a $130,000 payment made by Trump's former lawyer and fixer, Michael Cohen, to adult film performer Stormy Daniels shortly before the 2016 election. The payment was intended to secure her silence about an alleged sexual encounter with Trump approximately a decade earlier, which the president has consistently denied.Cohen was subsequently reimbursed by Trump's company in 2017, with the payments recorded as legal expenses.Prosecutors argued that the business records were deliberately falsified to conceal an alleged conspiracy to influence the election.Trump's lawyer Robert Giuffra Jr. maintained that Manhattan District Attorney Alvin Bragg's office had improperly relied on the Federal Election Campaign Act (FECA), arguing that federal election law could not form the basis of a state prosecution.CBS News reported that the defence also challenged the jury instructions, arguing that jurors should have been required to unanimously agree on the underlying crime that elevated the falsification charges to felonies.Another significant aspect of the appeal concerns evidence from Trump's first presidential term. His legal team argued that testimony involving former White House communications director Hope Hicks and Trump's social media posts should not have been presented to jurors because they involved official presidential conduct protected by immunity.Hicks had testified about discussions with Trump after the Daniels allegations became public in 2018. His lawyers maintained that the conversations concerned his responsibilities as president, including managing press inquiries.However, prosecutors disputed that interpretation. According to AP News, Steven Wu, representing Bragg's office, argued that the conversations reflected Trump's personal opinions rather than official presidential duties.The prosecution also maintained that even if certain evidence should have been excluded, its admission did not affect the overall outcome because substantial other evidence supported the conviction.The five-judge panel repeatedly interrupted both legal teams with questions about their arguments. One judge also questioned whether the cumulative admission of potentially improper evidence could still be considered harmless.CBS News noted that Trump's defence additionally challenged the requirement for jury unanimity on the underlying offences, while prosecutors pointed out that the trial defence had previously accepted the judge's approach.The May 2024 conviction followed a unanimous jury verdict. Trump was found guilty on all 34 counts but received no punishment that impeded his return to the White House.His attempts to shift the case from state to federal court meanwhile have also faced setbacks.A federal judge denied his immunity dismissal request for the third time in August, with another appeal scheduled for Nov. 16.The New York appeals court has not announced its decision, leaving Trump's historic conviction in limbo.Images Courtesy: istock and Instagram
Article Summary: Donald Trump was found guilty of 34 felony counts in May 2024. His legal team is attempting to have the historic verdict overturned. The latest challenge brought the President's lawyers face to face with a five-judge appeals panel, which closely examined questions surrounding presidential immunity, election laws and evidence presented during his trial.

Article Title: Kochi Mini Cooper crash: Kerala HC grants bail to all 4 accused; prime accused Suhail Sajeev to be released after 10 days
Article Text:
19-year-old, Suhail Sajeev prime accused in the Mini Cooper crash

(With Agency Inputs)





KOCHI: The Kerala High Court on Friday granted bail to four persons arrested in connection with the Nedumbassery Mini Cooper crash that claimed the lives of three youngsters. However, the court directed that the prime accused, Suhail Sajeev, be released only after 10 days.Justice Kauser Edappagath passed the order on bail petitions filed by Sajeev, Ninav, Joyal Anto and Ameen Shah, who were travelling in the Mini Cooper that rammed into a scooter carrying three youngsters, including two women, on the Nedumbassery airport road on October 11.The court deferred Sajeev's release by 10 days after taking into consideration the apprehensions raised by the prosecution and the counsel representing the deceased's families.Earlier, the Ernakulam District Sessions Court and the Angamaly Judicial First Class Magistrate Court had rejected the bail pleas of the four accused.During the hearing, the defence lawyers submitted that all four accused were 19-year-old students whose studies had been affected by their prolonged judicial custody.Opposing the bail pleas, the prosecution pointed out that the three victims were also youngsters from poor families and were the hopes of their respective families.The prosecution further submitted that, except Sajeev, the other accused had fled the scene soon after the accident and were subsequently arrested by the police.It argued that the investigation was still underway and would be completed at the earliest, but releasing the accused could affect the probe.The court observed that key aspects of the investigation, including allegations of drunken driving and overspeeding, had already been completed.It also noted that it could not be concluded that the accused had the requisite knowledge. Observing that they were young and had spent nearly a month in custody, the court considered their bail pleas.The prosecution and the counsel representing the deceased's families expressed apprehensions that Sajeev, who allegedly belonged to an influential family, could tamper with evidence if released.The counsel for the deceased's families also submitted that Sajeev had allegedly claimed soon after the accident that his father would take care of everything.However, the court observed that this alone could not be a ground to deny him bail.The counsel further alleged that Sajeev was a habitual high-speed driver and argued that granting him bail could send a negative message to society.After hearing the submissions, the court granted bail to all four accused, with the condition that Sajeev's release would be deferred by 10 days.
Article Summary: Kerala High Court grants bail to four persons arrested in Mini Cooper crash. However, the court directed that the prime accused, Suhail Sajeev, be released only after 10 days. The Mini Cooper rammed into a scooter carrying three youngsters, including two women, on the Nedumbassery airport road.

Article Title: ‘Accused’s claim wife’s family humiliated him’: Minister Priyank Kharge on Bengaluru family massacre
Article Text:
Priyank Kharge says killings appear pre-planned (R: Accused Indushekar)





BENGALURU: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge on Friday said the accused in the Bengaluru family massacre claimed he was humiliated by his wife's family, adding that the killings appeared to have been pre-planned.He said, "It is a very unfortunate incident and looks like it was pre-planned within the family,” news agency ANI reported.“The investigation is on. The accused claims that he was humiliated by his wife's side. It is definitely a twisted mind that has done the job. He has given the whereabouts of the bodies across the state," Kharge added further.The accused, identified as Indushekar, allegedly killed his wife Sunita, mother-in-law Roopavati, brothers-in-law Shivakumar and Shankar, their wives, both named Divya, and Shankar's seven-year-old son, Puneeth, police said.According to preliminary findings, the killings took place over two days at the accused's house on 59th Cross, near Bahsyam Circle, in Bengaluru's Srirampura locality. Police suspect a prolonged domestic dispute over Sunita's visits to her parental home may have led to the murders.Police said Indushekar allegedly first killed Sunita and dumped her body near Nandi Hills in Chikkaballapur district. He later invited his brothers-in-law to his house for a party and allegedly killed them, their wives, his mother-in-law and the seven-year-old boy.Police have so far recovered Puneeth's body.The remaining bodies are suspected to have been dumped at different locations in Bengaluru and neighbouring areas, including Chikkaballapur district. Police are continuing efforts to trace them.The accused allegedly used chemicals to clean the house and remove bloodstains after the killings.Police have seized the grinding stone suspected to have been used in the murders and the car allegedly used to transport the bodies.
Article Summary: Karnataka minister Priyank Kharge says killings appear pre-planned. Accused Indushekar claims he was humiliated by his wife's family. Police suspect a domestic dispute over Sunita's visits to her parental home may have led to the murders.

Article Title: Bengaluru road rage: Man follows woman to her friend’s apartment, attacks her with bucket
Article Text:
30-year-old woman named Meena experienced a violent attack in Banashankari after confronting a reckless driver (AI image)





BENGALURU: A narrow escape from a road accident turned into a terrifying ordeal for a 30-year-old woman in Banashankari when a scooter-borne man, whom she had confronted for driving on the wrong side, allegedly chased her to friend’s apartment and launched a vicious attack. He allegedly hit her with a hard object and an empty paint bucket, targeting her head, shoulder, arms and face, while hurling obscene and derogatory abuses.According to the complaint filed by Meena (name changed), a research scholar and resident of Banashankari 3rd Stage, the incident occurred at 10am on Oct 30. She had gone for a workout at a gym and was riding her scooter towards her friend’s apartment when the incident unfolded.On the way, a man riding a scooter with a woman as pillion allegedly approached at high speed from the wrong direction and nearly rammed into her vehicle. Meena narrowly avoided the collision and questioned him over his reckless driving. After the argument, Meena continued towards her friend’s apartment. However, the man allegedly followed her. Even after she reached the apartment and parked her scooter outside, he approached her and assaulted her.She told him not to come near her and rushed inside the apartment. Carrying a bag containing an object, he followed her inside. He attacked her several times on the head, shoulder, arm and forearm, leaving her injured.Even as the man’s wife reportedly tried to restrain him, he picked up an empty paint bucket and struck Meena on the face and neck. The commotion eventually drew the attention of residents and Meena’s friend, who rushed to the spot around 10.15am and questioned the man about his actions. He then stopped the attack and left the apartment complex.Traumatised by the incident, Meena sought medical treatment and filed a complaint on Nov 3.Channammanakere Achukattu police registered a case under Sections 79 (word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman), 118 (voluntarily causing hurt or grievous hurt by dangerous weapons or means) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace).An officer said CCTV footage from the locations where the accused allegedly followed Meena and from the apartment complex was being examined.
Article Summary: 30-year-old woman attacked in Banashankari after confronting a reckless driver. He allegedly hit her with a hard object and an empty paint bucket, targeting her head, shoulder, arms and face, while hurling obscene and derogatory abuses. Police registered a case under Sections 79 (word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman) and 352 (intentional insult with intent to provoke breach of peace)
